findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff uses dark-light-choose() in the embedded stylesheet, but the embed pipeline compiles against a minimal variable/function set and does not load the common color-definition mixins that define dark-light-choose for the interactive stylesheets. If the function is not defined in the embed compile context, `rake assets:precompile` / the embed stylesheet build fails with "Undefined operation / undefined function dark-light-choose", breaking embedded topics on any site that builds assets after this change.

[BUG] The light-theme branch was silently changed from 30% to 70% lightness — the diff changes light-theme behavior, not just adds a dark-theme branch. In light color schemes, the small-action link (e.g. reply/like counts in .small-action .float-kit area) renders with scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) — a much lighter, low-contrast grey instead of the previous dark 30% value; users on light themes lose legible link text.

[BUG] The light-theme value of .custom-message-length was changed from 70% to 30%, inverting the original light-theme styling while the identical desktop rule in desktop/modal.scss keeps 70%. On mobile with a light color scheme, the custom message length hint renders dark (30%) instead of light (70%), diverging from desktop and from the pre-change appearance; mobile light-theme users see harsher, heavier hint text in modals.

[BUG] The light-theme branch for the small-action h3 was changed from 20% to 50% lightness, altering light-theme output rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative. Mobile light-scheme users see the small-action heading at 50% lightness — noticeably lighter and lower contrast than the previous near-black 20% value — regressing readability of mobile small-action headings.

[BUG] The .name light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 50% while the adjacent .title kept its original 50% value, changing light-theme behavior. On desktop light schemes, the user card's display name now renders at the same 50% lightness as the title instead of the previous darker 30%, reducing visual hierarchy and contrast for names on user cards.

[BUG] The .name light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 50%, altering the light-theme rendering rather than only adding the dark-theme branch. On mobile light schemes the user card display name drops to 50% lightness, matching the title color and losing the previous darker emphasis; the change is inconsistent with the untouched desktop common/base/user.scss equivalent (30%→70% pattern).

[BUG] The light-theme value of .custom-message-length was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), silently altering light themes instead of only adding a dark variant. On light themes the character-count hint under the custom message composer on mobile becomes near-black instead of dim gray, clashing with its 85% font size and diverging from desktop's identical rule (desktop/modal.scss line 99 keeps 70%) — the PR title promises dark-theme-only changes, so this is an unreviewed regression of light-theme styling.

[BUG] The h3 link color's light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) inside dark-light-choose, breaking the pattern used everywhere else in the diff of preserving the original light value. On light-theme mobile, the small-action heading link (e.g. 'topic closed by moderator' banners) becomes 50% lightness instead of 20%, i.e. noticeably fainter than the desktop counterpart which keeps 20% (desktop/topic-post.scss uses (20%, 80%)) — mobile and desktop render the same element with different colors.

[BUG] The small-action bold link's light-theme value was changed from 30% to 70% lightness: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) swaps the percentages relative to the 30%/70% convention used by every other 30% conversion in this diff. On light themes the bolded link in the small-action notice (e.g. 'No more messages' / close notices) renders at 70% lightness — barely visible washed-out gray — instead of the intended near-black 30%; on dark themes it renders 30% secondary instead of 70%, so both branches are wrong for this rule.

[BUG] The user-card .name light-theme value was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), silently altering light-theme rendering. On light themes the display name on the user profile page/card loses its 30%-lightness emphasis and renders at the same 50% gray as .title beneath it, flattening the visual hierarchy the old rule established; the PR title states only dark themes use $secondary, so this light-theme change is unrequested drift.

[BUG] The mobile user-card .name light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50% lightness, mirroring an unintended change rather than preserving the original light value as done for every other 30% rule in the diff. On light-theme mobile the profile display name renders at 50% gray instead of the previous 30% near-black, matching the .title below it and erasing the name's visual weight; dark-theme value of 50% secondary is also out of family with the 70% convention used for other 30% rules.

[ADVISORY] The same touched rule block leaves .wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); } and the disabled inputs' new dark-light-choose background unpaired, skipping the dark-light-choose treatment for the editor text color. On dark themes the disabled .wmd-input background now correctly flips to scale-color($secondary, 25%), but the enabled .wmd-input text color still uses darken($primary, 40%), which on a dark $primary (e.g. #222) computes to near-black text on a dark background — the composer input becomes unreadable, and this line is the only dark-theme-naive primitive left in the converted block.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of a.title was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), altering light-theme appearance despite the PR's stated intent of only adding dark-theme handling. Light-theme users see quote/reply usernames rendered at 70% lightness instead of 30%, a visible regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix the PR claims to implement.

[BUG] The light-theme value of .custom-message-length was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), diverging from the desktop/modal.scss equivalent (which keeps 70%) and changing light-theme output. Mobile light-theme users get a darker, harder-to-read character-count hint than before, and the mobile/desktop stylesheets for the same element now disagree on the light branch; anyone expecting a pure dark-theme change is bitten.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of h3 was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), modifying light-theme styling rather than only adding a dark variant. Mobile light-theme link titles inside posts lose their strong 20%-lightness emphasis and render washed out at 50%, a visual regression invisible to review intent 'only dark themes change'.

[BUG] The light-theme value of the user card .name was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), changing light-theme appearance outside the stated intent. Desktop light-theme user names in the summary panel render dimmer than before; the change is not traceable to the 'dark themes only' requirement.

[BUG] The light-theme value of the user .name was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), altering light-theme styling outside the stated dark-theme-only intent. Mobile light-theme user names lose their 30%-lightness contrast and render at 50%, a silent light-theme visual change smuggled into a dark-theme fix.

[BUG] The `.topic-map .links a` (bold link) rule silently changes the light-theme value: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`, altering the primary-branch lightness from 30% to 70% when every other conversion in this diff preserves the original lightness. Light-theme users see these bold topic-map links washed out (70% lightness instead of 30%), breaking the intended high-emphasis styling; dark-theme conversion also inverts the emphasis relationship (primary 70% is dimmer than the surrounding 50% text).

[BUG] `.custom-message-length` was converted with both lightness values inverted relative to the original: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, whereas the desktop twin (desktop/modal.scss line 94) uses (70%, 30%) and the original was 70%. The mobile custom-message-length hint renders at 30% primary lightness on light themes (near-black instead of the intended muted 70%) and the mobile/desktop pair of the same element now drifts apart, so the same UI element has visibly different styling per device.

[BUG] The small-action `h3` rule changes the light-theme value: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, replacing the original 20% primary with 50% in the light branch instead of preserving it (compare the desktop twin at desktop/topic-post.scss line 321, which correctly uses 20%/80%). Mobile small-action headings lose their strong contrast on light themes and diverge from the desktop equivalent, so the same heading renders bold-dark on desktop but mid-gray on mobile.

[BUG] The user-card `.name` rule changes the light-theme value: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of preserving 30% (the `.username a` sibling two rules up correctly uses 30%/70%). Desktop user-card display names on light themes render mid-gray (50%) instead of the intended high-contrast 30%, so the name loses its designed visual weight and no longer matches the username color beside it.

[BUG] The mobile user-card `.name` rule changes the light-theme value: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` instead of preserving 30% as the desktop twin does. Mobile user-card names lose contrast on light themes (50% vs intended 30%) and diverge from the desktop rendering of the identical element.

[ADVISORY] The coldmap/heatmap color ramp is converted to `dark-light-choose` only for coldmap classes while `heatmap-high` remains hardcoded `#fe7a15`, and the dark-branch ramp uses secondary lightness 30/40/50 stepping in the same direction as the light branch rather than a reviewed coldness ramp for dark themes. Dark-theme users get an unvalidated color ramp on the topic heat/age indicators; the step ordering was derived mechanically (100−lightness) rather than tested for perceptual monotonicity on dark backgrounds, so the 'colder = dimmer' comment above the block may no longer hold on dark themes.

[BUG] The light-theme value was silently changed from 30% to 70% lightness instead of only adding the dark-theme branch: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)` replaced `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. In light themes, the bold username links in the small-action row (e.g. 'topic closed by X' lines) render at 70% lightness instead of 30%, making them pale and low-contrast against the background — a visible regression in the light theme that goes beyond the PR's stated intent of fixing dark themes.

[BUG] The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50% lightness: `.name`'s `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, altering the first argument rather than only adding a dark branch. User profile display names on desktop light themes lose their stronger (30%) contrast and render at the same muted 50% tone as the title line, flattening the intended visual hierarchy without any stated requirement for a light-theme change.

[BUG] The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50% lightness for the profile `.name` element: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became the first argument `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` of dark-light-choose. Mobile light-theme profile display names drop from 30% to 50% lightness, silently changing light-theme rendering that the PR (dark-theme fix) never asked to change.

[BUG] The light-theme value was inverted from 70% to 30%: `.custom-message-length`'s `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, swapping which branch gets which value. Mobile light-theme custom-message-length hints render at 30% lightness (near-full-contrast, heavy dark text) instead of the intended subtle 70%, a visible light-theme regression; the desktop/modal.scss counterpart kept 70%/30%, so the two now disagree.

[BUG] The light-theme value was changed from 20% to 50% lightness for the embedded/small-action `h3`: `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, modifying the light branch instead of leaving it untouched. Mobile light-theme h3 headings (e.g. deleted-post notices) that were intentionally near-primary (20% lightness) now render at the muted 50% tone, reducing prominence — a light-theme change with no basis in the PR's dark-theme objective.

[BUG] The refactor silently changes the light theme value for .names a from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), a value change unrelated to the dark-theme fix the PR claims. Light-theme usernames in the post stream render at 70% lightness instead of the intended 30%, producing washed-out, nearly invisible username links on light color schemes; whoever audits this PR for dark-theme-only changes misses the regression because the diff pattern looks mechanical.

[BUG] The h3 color changes the light-theme value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), silently altering light-theme heading contrast instead of only adding the dark-theme alternative. Mobile users on light color schemes see the small-post h3 title at 50% lightness instead of the previous 20%, significantly reducing contrast and readability — a regression the PR description never mentions and nothing in the diff verifies.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length light-theme value is inverted from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), whereas the equivalent desktop/modal.scss rule keeps 70%. Mobile modals render the custom message length hint at 30% lightness (near-foreground, high contrast) instead of the previous subtle 70%, and the desktop/mobile pair for the identical selector now diverges (desktop 70% vs mobile 30%), so mobile and desktop show different hint styling for the same component.

[BUG] The .name light-theme value is changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while the adjacent .title rule stays at 50%, changing the deliberate name/title visual hierarchy. On light themes the user profile card's name loses its intended 30%-lightness emphasis and becomes identical to the .title's 50%, flattening the hierarchy; the change is unrelated to the PR's stated dark-theme purpose.

[BUG] Same unintended light-theme change as desktop: .name goes from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), matching .title and erasing the hierarchy. Mobile user profile cards show the display name at 50% lightness instead of 30%, identical to the title beneath it — a silent light-theme regression decoupled from the dark-light-choose migration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `dark-light-choose(...)` into `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` (e.g., `a.new-user { color: dark-light-choose(...) }`). However, the claim that the embed stylesheet compiles in a context where `dark-light-choose` is undefined cannot be verified from the diff alone (it depends on the asset pipeline/load order outside this patch). This is a concrete compatibility risk raised by the change, but not a verifiable, certain break based solely on the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same touched rule block leaves .wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); } and the disabled inputs' new dark-light-choose background unpaired, skipping the dark-light-choose treatment for the editor text color. On dark themes the disabled .wmd-input background now correctly flips to scale-color($secondary, 25%), but the enabled .wmd-input text color still uses darken($primary, 40%), which on a dark $primary (e.g. #222) computes to near-black text on a dark background — the composer input becomes unreadable, and this line is the only dark-theme-naive primitive left in the converted block.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss`, the diff updates disabled editor backgrounds to `dark-light-choose(...)` (`#reply-title:disabled` and `.wmd-input:disabled`), but leaves the enabled `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` unchanged and not theme-aware. The claim that this definitively becomes unreadable in dark themes depends on how `$primary`/background are defined (not shown in the diff), so the concrete, verifiable point is an incomplete dark/light conversion in the same area rather than a proven functional break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme branch of a.title was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), altering light-theme appearance despite the PR's stated intent of only adding dark-theme handling. Light-theme users see quote/reply usernames rendered at 70% lightness instead of 30%, a visible regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix the PR claims to implement.

[BUG] The light-theme value of .custom-message-length was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), diverging from the desktop/modal.scss equivalent (which keeps 70%) and changing light-theme output. Mobile light-theme users get a darker, harder-to-read character-count hint than before, and the mobile/desktop stylesheets for the same element now disagree on the light branch; anyone expecting a pure dark-theme change is bitten.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` changes from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. This means the light-theme branch (first argument to `dark-light-choose`) is now `$primary` at 30% lightness instead of 70%. In contrast, `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss` updates the same selector to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`, preserving 70% for light theme. The diff therefore introduces a mobile/desktop inconsistency and a light-theme color regression on mobile for this element.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The coldmap/heatmap color ramp is converted to `dark-light-choose` only for coldmap classes while `heatmap-high` remains hardcoded `#fe7a15`, and the dark-branch ramp uses secondary lightness 30/40/50 stepping in the same direction as the light branch rather than a reviewed coldness ramp for dark themes. Dark-theme users get an unvalidated color ramp on the topic heat/age indicators; the step ordering was derived mechanically (100−lightness) rather than tested for perceptual monotonicity on dark backgrounds, so the 'colder = dimmer' comment above the block may no longer hold on dark themes.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/discourse.scss, only the .coldmap-* classes were changed to use dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30/40/50)), while .heatmap-high remains a hardcoded #fe7a15. The finding’s broader claim about perceptual monotonicity/"untested" ramps can’t be verified from the diff, but it is diff-grounded that the dark-branch values appear to be a mechanically inverted set (70→30, 60→40, 50→50) and that the heatmap ramp wasn’t converted, which is a reasonable theming-consistency concern rather than a provable functional break.
